A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSVAE research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Content can be matched across the substantial reordering and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation and reconstruction experiments, spectral analyses, component ablations, and hyperparameter studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds human-preference results, reconstruction tests, public-data validation, and further diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: The architecture and core LCR/LMR components remain. However, the reported final training stage changes: v1 specifies 2×2×2 masking with revised probabilities during 512p decoder finetuning, whereas v2 Section 5.2 explicitly disables both regularizers. This is a limited revision to the stated training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds DAVIS reconstruction evaluation and downstream image-to-video generation with first-frame conditioning. Appendix A.4 also trains diffusion models on COYO, LAION, and Panda70M; these public datasets previously supported VAE training, while diffusion training used private film/TV clips. These additions broaden task and training-data coverage.

E2.justification: The main generation comparator set and the SER, VA-VAE, and CPR comparisons are retained. v2 Tables 5–6 add a retrained Wan 2.2 VAE as a reconstruction control, extending the evaluated comparison variants.

E3.justification: Beyond revising the 512p regularization schedule, v2 introduces a 1,200-pair human-preference evaluation, public-data diffusion training for 100k steps at 512p, image-to-video first-frame PSNR, and DINO-affinity and corruption-residual diagnostics. These substantially expand evaluation procedures. The revised training description does not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled reconstruction ablations, DINO structural-affinity analysis, CPR/LMR corruption-residual analysis, and measured regularizer overhead. It extends incremental component analysis to VBench and adds generation-quality measurements to the existing LCR hyperparameter study. These provide substantial new tests of fidelity, mechanisms, and efficiency.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new user-study pair count describes evaluation size rather than repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the 512p Baseline FVD from 770 to 970 on VBench and 581 to 681 on MovieGenBench, reversing its displayed ordering against SSVAE. Reconstruction PSNR/LPIPS change from 37.51/0.0339 to 37.84/0.0325 alongside revised finetuning. The LMR-study baseline changes from UR 39.0/FVD 472 to 39.2/471. v2 also adds a 55.7% human win rate and extensive new results; its Figure 2(b) replaces v1's diffusion-loss curves with FVD curves.

T1.justification: The principal theorem, its proof, and the LCR autocorrelation derivation are retained. Appendix A.1 adds mathematical reasoning about linear noising with affine prediction targets and explains that epsilon-prediction yields isotropic target-input cross-correlation, limiting this diagnostic's ability to distinguish latent modes.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same two spectral properties, lightweight LCR/LMR regularizers, backbone independence, 3× convergence speedup, and 10% reward improvement. Reordering the spectral discussion and adding supporting experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation of reconstruction tradeoffs, arguing that latent smoothness need not remove RGB detail and attributing LMR's fidelity cost to precision versus robustness. It discusses capacity/training explanations for the Wan reconstruction gap, distinguishes LCR's structural-affinity effects from LMR's spectral role, and interprets residual-mode diagnostics. It also acknowledges mixed 256p FVD and qualifies applicability under epsilon-prediction.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents batch-level LCR and application of L1, LPIPS, and GAN losses to masked reconstructions. It adds VAE parameter counts, per-step timing measurements, and supplementary-video folder references. These improve technical disclosure, although detailed human-study and timing configurations remain sparse; the code link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bonnaire et al. on diffusion-training dynamics, Ge et al. on FVD content bias, and Seaweed-7B for training-budget context. It also refines positioning relative to structural representation regularization. The main related-work framework and novelty claims remain.

P1.justification: v2 places channel eigenspectrum shaping before frequency shaping and revises the abstract and introduction accordingly. It moves the CPR comparison into the LMR discussion, reorganizes reconstruction analysis within the ablations, and restructures the supplement. These are substantial narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout with extensive figure and table rearrangement. v1 Figures 5 and 7 become v2 Figure 3, while Figures 2 and 3 become Figure 4. New preference and reconstruction panels, expanded ablation tables, and supplementary diagnostic displays substantially change presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation: human preferences supplement automated rewards, public-data diffusion training addresses dependence on private training data, and controlled reconstruction, DAVIS/I2V, and overhead studies test important fidelity and efficiency concerns left weakly supported in v1. Added mechanism and applicability qualifications improve interpretation. Sparse study details and unexplained baseline FVD revisions remain limitations, but the complementary evidence provides a substantial overall quality gain.
